newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates up on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates up on weekend covering.

text.p: * Central Bank closes reverse repos, special T-bills
Philippine interbank offered rates were slightly higher on Monday as banks covered three days of weekend positions, traders said.
The average rate nudged up to 11.34375 from 11.125 percent, with done rates ranging from 12.25 to 11.0625 percent.
But turnover was smaller than expected at 19.772 from 23.773 billion pesos, indicating the market was liquid, a trader said.
Traders said banks' positions were helped by the closure of the Central Bank of its reverse repo and special series T-bill facilities since Friday.
"That resulted in a lot of money lying around," a trader said.
But the Central Bank is expected to open these on Tuesday.
Rates are expected to ease in the next session when banks cover positions for Monday when 4.9 billion pesos worth of T-notes are expected to have matured.
They added another 5.1 to 3.6 billion pesos are also expected to return to banks from maturng T-bills in midweek.

In the secondary market trading of T-bills, there was no active positioning by banks due to the holidays as a result of the summit meeting of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), traders said.
"Trading was only limited to short-term tenors for the servicing of corporate requirements," said a big bank dealer.
The three-month rate bills had bids of 11.70 to 11.875 percent; the six months at 12.35 to 12.50; and the one year at 12.75 to 12.875 percent, dealers said.
